input.summary:
P3 rear bedroom furnished in parts/room-29.mjs: one red bed on the east wall (focal, opposite the west door), barrel-and-chest dresser on the north partition, oak-post nightstand with a standing lantern, lit candle on the chest, flower pot on a barrel.
make.sh runs whole with 9 cells placed, no REFUSED or off-palette lines; `mcd room` says OK (9/9 reachable, min light 11, 0 dark) and the rooms render reads as a bedroom.
Walk lane is the middle row z19 from the door to the bed; my cells have no check warnings (the check output's other warnings are outside my box).
left: The spec says the door is at (58,6..7,19), but the plan grid and the room check put the doorway in the west wall at x57 z19; I furnished to the grid, so the lane is unaffected.
No rug (carpet) was added; the room has no need for it at this size, and I kept the lane clear.
plan.md's checklist and elements.md were not ticked: they track the row-level and house-level items, and the rear bedroom covers only one bed and the lighting of its own cells.

waste.what: Worked out which wall cells are doorways, windows and solid by reading the plan grid, then checked each by the room tool after the build
waste.cost: about 2 extra make and room runs
waste.tool: mcd plan should mark the doorway cell the spec names (door x58 vs grid x57) and print the wall side each opening lies on

waste.what: Placed the bed by coordinates I worked out by hand (foot x59, head x60 against the x61 wall, facing east)
waste.tool: a bedSet-like helper that takes the wall to lie against and finds the foot and head itself from the plan's free cells

waste.what: Drew the furniture as two y layers of text and had to fix one row by hand (a stray letter not in the legend)
waste.cost: one retry on the top layer
waste.tool: layers() could report characters not in its legend, instead of skipping them silently

companions.task: Confirm the lantern placement under the ceiling once the attic and roof above the rear bedroom are final, so the lantern can hang from a beam instead of standing on the nightstand.
